memory_update.text: CHEF is the cleanest underfollowed specialty-distribution candidate for the restaurant route-density node: specialty foods, center-of-the-plate products, chef/customer relationships, distribution centers, and delivery fleet.

WEST is a small-cap category-specialist candidate for coffee/tea/beverage supply into restaurants, foodservice, c-stores, hospitality, and travel centers; thesis depends on margin conversion and capacity utilization.

HFFG is a high-purity but below-USD-300M speculative exception for Asian restaurant distribution; next layers must heavily penalize governance, internal controls, losses, related-party exposure, and cash conversion if not improving.

Need a dedicated follow-up search for publicly listed route-based coffee DSD and bakery/produce/protein specialists; FARM appears highly relevant operationally but too small and financially distressed to rank as a core candidate without stronger evidence.

For this node, the key chokepoint variables are not brand power but route density, fill-rate reliability, cold-chain handling, category-specific sourcing, customer stickiness, labor/fuel pass-through, private-label or specialty mix, and acquisition integration discipline.

node: Specialty foodservice distribution and route-density logistics
summary: Layer 1B expands the specialty foodservice distribution node beyond obvious broadline distributors. The best underfollowed lane appears to be route-dense category specialists: premium restaurant ingredients, Asian restaurant supply, coffee/beverage DSD, and private-label coffee/tea solutions. PFGC is included only as a large-cap reference anchor for route-density economics and segment disclosure; the main discovery candidates are CHEF, WEST, HFFG, and FARM-style businesses, with HFFG/FARM treated as speculative shadow candidates because their market caps are below the preferred USD 300M floor and carry financial/control-risk flags.
